newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran to build two gas storage units for $700 mln.
newsitem.headline: Iran to build two gas storage units for $700 mln.

text.p: OPEC-member Iran plans to build two underground facilities worth up to $700 million to store natural gas near Tehran, a senior Iranian official said in remarks published on Thursday.

Deputy Oil Minister Hamdollah Mohammad-Nejad said excavation work on one of the facilities, outside Varamin 50 km (30 miles) southeast of Tehran, would start next week, the daily Hamshahri newspaper reported.
The second storage facility, outside Qom 120 km (75 miles) south of the capital, was under study and design, he said.
The facilities, each with a capacity of one million cubic metres (35.3 million cubic feet) would be built for $300 million to $350 million each supplied by the Oil Ministry, Mohammad-Nejad added.

He said authorities would draw on the gas stocks "in times when it is needed", in apparent reference to periods of high consumption when Tehran's domestic gas distribution and power network has suffered from shortages.
Iran holds the world's second largest gas reserves after Russia but most of its natural gas is in the south of the country, far from Tehran and other large population centres in the north.
